EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Here’s Your Chance To Buy a Six-Wheel Drive Mercedes G-Class!
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Of course there’s a catch, because this thing did not start life in this configuration, as it was a 2017 Mercedes-Benz G 550 4x4 Squared when it first came out, and it has Esteem Customs to thank four the 6x6 conversion.
Thus, the third Mercedes-Benz portal axle, as well as the 22-inch Vossen wheels shod in 37-inch M/T tires, the KW racing coilovers, upgraded brakes, and the custom extended chassis and rear bed bodywork have come from the aftermarket realm.
The same goes for the Brabus-style front grille and carbon fiber dual snorkels, as well as the hood, fender covers, flares, door mirror casings, and trim molding, all of which have been made of carbon fiber. The front and rear skid plates, the metal rear bumper guard, power running boards, and exhaust system are other modifications mentioned in the listing. The head unit, Brabus-style blue interior, and floor mats round off the makeover.
Power is supplied by a V8 engine, which is said to have a 4.0-liter displacement. The mill is twin turbocharged, and according to the listing, develops 416 hp (422 ps/310 kW) and 450 pound-feet (610 Nm) of torque. Everything is channeled to all six wheels through a seven-speed automatic transmission, and a two-speed transfer case. The ad also mentions the independent differential locks, and the portal axles for enhanced off-roading prowess.
Photo: Cars&Bids This older Mercedes-Benz G 550 4x4 Squared that has become a veritable 6x6 is presented in Designo Manufaktur Sintered Bronze Magno, on top of a blue interior. It features a Harman Kardon sound system, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility, Bluetooth connectivity, and other stuff that is mentioned in the ad.
Care to talk about the known flaws? Well, a TPMS (tire pressure monitoring system) light is illuminated. And that’s not all, because the Carfax report reveals that this six-wheel drive beast sustained “minor” damage to the front end as a result of a collision with a vehicle recorded at the end of 2024. However, the airbags did not deploy during the accident.
The six-wheel drive Mercedes G-Wagen in question is said to have had all portal axles serviced, as well as all differentials, and the rear transfer case. The rear driveshafts were replaced and balanced, and the engine oil and filter were changed, the selling dealer reported.
According to the ad, the vendor bought this G-Class earlier in 2026, adding some 2,000 miles (3,200 km) since. The vehicle had around 8,000 miles (12,800 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging. It is accompanied by the paint-matched fiberglass fender flares, and one key, and you can find it on Cars&Bids here , as part of an online auction that will end on November 30, 2026. The highest bid was $105,000 at the time of writing. How much is this ride worth to you?
